entries.khalafReading: Contextual ta'wil: istiwa over the Throne is rendered as Allah's absolute dominion and subjugation, never sitting, spatial establishment or movement. Allah's attribute of subjugation is not temporally originated.

entries.englishMeaning: He directs the affair from heaven to earth; then the matter is raised for His judgment in a day whose measure is a thousand years by your reckoning.
entries.editorialNote: The ascent is rendered without locating Allah at a spatial destination.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the ascent wording while denying that Allah occupies a destination, place or direction to which created things physically travel.
entries.khalafReading: Ascent is read contextually as being raised by Allah's command, to His acceptance, judgment or an appointed station, without locating Allah.

entries.englishMeaning: Then He fashioned him and caused the created spirit honoured by Him to enter him; and appointed for you hearing and sight and hearts. Small thanks give ye!
entries.editorialNote: Possessive/from-Him spirit language is rendered as a created spirit, an attribution of honour, command or divine support; it never means a part, soul or component of Allah.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the revealed wording according to a meaning befitting Allah while maintaining tanzih: Allah does not resemble creation and is not described by body, limbs, composition, place, direction, movement, change, or a created modality.
entries.khalafReading: Contextual ta’wil: the spirit is created and may be attributed to Allah by honour, command, creation or support; Allah is not composed of parts and has no soul.

entries.englishMeaning: So taste the consequence: because you neglected the meeting of this Day, today We leave you to its punishment. Taste the lasting punishment for what you used to do.
entries.editorialNote: The baseline 'We forget you' is replaced because literal forgetfulness is an impossible deficiency for Allah.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the revealed wording while categorically denying forgetfulness, ignorance, lapse, change or any deficiency in Allah.
entries.khalafReading: Contextual ta'wil: divine 'forgetting' here means leaving them in punishment and withholding favour as just requital, not loss of knowledge or memory.

entries.englishMeaning: Say: If I err, I err only against myself; and if I am guided, it is by what my Lord reveals to me. Surely He is All-Hearing and near by His knowledge and response.
entries.editorialNote: Divine qurb is rendered non-spatially through knowledge and response, not physical nearness or location.
entries.salafReading: Affirm divine nearness with a meaning befitting Allah while denying distance, physical proximity, contact, indwelling or location.
entries.khalafReading: Contextual ta'wil: nearness is understood through Allah's knowledge and response, not spatial distance.

entries.englishMeaning: Whoever seeks honour, then all honour belongs to Allah. Good words are accepted by Him, and He raises the righteous deed in rank. Those who plot evil will have a severe punishment, and their plotting will fail.
entries.editorialNote: The supplied guide identifies this verse as mutashabih and requires any assigned meaning to comply with Arabic, the Religion and the muhkam foundations. 'Good words are accepted by Him' prevents a spatial reading of ascent to a location. This wording remains subject to named scholarly review.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the revealed wording with a meaning befitting Allah while denying spatial movement or location.
entries.khalafReading: A contextual reading treats the ascent of good words as their acceptance and honouring by Allah, not movement toward a place occupied by Him.

entries.englishMeaning: Indeed, Allah preserves the heavens and the earth from ceasing or deviating. If they were to cease, no one after Him could preserve them. Surely He is Most Forbearing, Most Forgiving.
entries.editorialNote: The Pickthall baseline uses 'graspeth'. Arabic yumsiku is rendered as preserves/restrains here so the English does not suggest a bodily grasp or hand.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the revealed wording according to a meaning befitting Allah while maintaining tanzih: Allah does not resemble creation and is not described by body, limbs, composition, place, direction, movement, change, or any created modality.
entries.khalafReading: Contextual ta'wil: Allah preserves and restrains the heavens and earth by His power; no bodily grasp, limb or instrument is implied.

entries.englishMeaning: Have they not seen that We created for them, by Our power, livestock of which they are owners?
entries.editorialNote: The Arabic expression ma 'amilat aydina is rendered through divine power and creation, not bodily hands or created instruments.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the revealed expression with a meaning befitting Allah while denying limbs, hands, bodily parts, composition, or created instruments.
entries.khalafReading: Contextual ta'wil: aydina here is rendered through Allah's power and creative act, not bodily hands.

entries.englishMeaning: So glory be to Him Who has absolute dominion over all things, and to Him you will be returned.
entries.editorialNote: Bi-yadihi is rendered as dominion, avoiding a bodily-hand reading.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the revealed expression with a meaning befitting Allah while denying limbs, hands, parts, bodily form or created instruments.
entries.khalafReading: Yad and related expressions are read contextually as power, authority, generosity, care or disposal according to the verse, not as bodily hands.

entries.englishMeaning: And Ibrahim said: I am going to where my Lord has commanded me; He will guide me.
entries.editorialNote: The supplied guide rejects the literalist inference that Ibrahim was travelling to a country in which Allah is located. SalahOS makes the commanded destination explicit rather than implying movement toward Allah's place.
entries.salafReading: The wording is affirmed without attributing place, direction or spatial location to Allah.
entries.khalafReading: The journey is understood as going where Allah commanded Ibrahim to go; Allah is not located in the destination.

entries.englishMeaning: When I have fashioned him and placed within him a created spirit honored by Me, then fall down before him in prostration.
entries.editorialNote: My Spirit is an attribution of honor to a created soul, not a part of Allah.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the possessive attribution while denying that Allah has a soul, spirit, part or anything separable from Him.
entries.khalafReading: Ruh attributed to Allah is a created spirit or angel honored by attribution to Him, not a part of Allah.

entries.englishMeaning: He said: O Iblis, what prevented you from prostrating to the one I created with special care? Were you arrogant, or were you among the exalted?
entries.editorialNote: The supplied guide explains yadayn in this verse by Allah's care and rejects a bodily-hands reading.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the revealed wording with a befitting meaning while denying limbs, hands, parts or bodily form.
entries.khalafReading: The guide gives the specific meaning of care for yadayn in this verse.
entries.guideSpecificMeaning: The care of Allah.

entries.englishMeaning: Lest any soul should say: Alas for my grief that I neglected my duty toward Allah, and I was indeed among the scoffers!
entries.editorialNote: Janb Allah is rendered as duty/right owed toward Allah rather than a bodily side.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the revealed wording according to a meaning befitting Allah while maintaining tanzih: Allah does not resemble creation and is not described by body, limbs, composition, place, direction, movement, change, or a created modality.
entries.khalafReading: Contextual ta’wil: janb denotes duty, right or obedience toward Allah, not a bodily side.

entries.englishMeaning: They did not esteem Allah as He deserves to be esteemed. On the Day of Resurrection the whole earth will be under His absolute power, and the heavens will be folded by His power. Glory be to Him, exalted above what they associate with Him.
entries.editorialNote: Qabdah and yamin are rendered through divine power rather than a handful or right hand.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the revealed expression with a meaning befitting Allah while denying limbs, hands, parts, bodily form or created instruments.
entries.khalafReading: Yad and related expressions are read contextually as power, authority, generosity, care or disposal according to the verse, not as bodily hands.

entries.englishMeaning: And the earth will shine with the illumination bestowed by its Lord; the Record will be set forth, the prophets and witnesses will be brought, and judgment will be given between them in truth, and they will not be wronged.
entries.editorialNote: The rendering avoids implying that Allah is a physical source of created luminosity.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the revealed wording according to a meaning befitting Allah while maintaining tanzih: Allah does not resemble creation and is not described by body, limbs, composition, place, direction, movement, change, or a created modality.
entries.khalafReading: Contextual ta’wil: the light is illumination created or bestowed by Allah, not Allah being physical light.

entries.englishMeaning: Then He directed His will to the heaven while it was smoke, and said to it and to the earth: Come willingly or unwillingly. They said: We come willingly.
entries.editorialNote: Istiwa ila is rendered as directing the divine will, not movement toward a spatial destination.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the revealed istiwa with a meaning befitting Allah while denying sitting, place, direction, movement, bodily form or any created modality.
entries.khalafReading: Where context permits, istiwa is explained non-spatially through dominion/subjugation or directing creation; it is never physical establishment or movement.

entries.englishMeaning: Indeed, they are in doubt about meeting their Lord. Surely Allah's knowledge encompasses all things.
entries.editorialNote: The supplied guide rejects a spatial reading in which Allah physically surrounds creation and gives the meaning that Allah knows everything.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the wording while denying bodily surrounding, enclosure, spatial extension or location.
entries.khalafReading: The guide gives the specific meaning: Allah knows everything.
entries.guideSpecificMeaning: Allah knows everything.

entries.englishMeaning: He is the Creator of the heavens and the earth. He made for you mates from yourselves and pairs among the livestock, multiplying you thereby. Absolutely nothing resembles Him. He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.
entries.editorialNote: The supplied guide treats 'Absolutely there is nothing like Him' as a governing muhkam foundation. All mutashabih renderings are checked against this principle.
entries.guideSpecificMeaning: Absolutely there is nothing like Him.

entries.englishMeaning: He alone is Allah, worshipped in the heaven and on the earth. He is the Wise, the Knower.
entries.editorialNote: Spatial/fawq wording is rendered through worship, authority, dominion or subjugation so the English does not place Allah inside creation or in a physical direction.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the revealed wording according to a meaning befitting Allah while maintaining tanzih: Allah does not resemble creation and is not described by body, limbs, composition, place, direction, movement, change, or a created modality.
entries.khalafReading: Contextual ta’wil: the verse is read through Allah’s authority, dominion, subjugation or being the One worshipped, not bodily location, containment, height or direction.

entries.englishMeaning: It will be said: Today We abandon you to your consequence, just as you neglected the meeting of this Day. Your refuge is the Fire, and you will have no helpers.
entries.editorialNote: Nisyan is rendered as abandonment in recompense, consistent with the muhkam statement that the Lord is never forgetful.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the revealed recompense wording while denying forgetfulness, ignorance or deficiency for Allah.
entries.khalafReading: Nisyan attributed in recompense is read as abandoning them to punishment or withholding mercy after they neglected His commands, not literal forgetfulness.

entries.englishMeaning: Do not lose heart or call for peace while you have the upper hand. Allah supports you and will not diminish the reward of your deeds.
entries.editorialNote: Ma'iyyah is rendered as support.
entries.salafReading: Affirm divine ma'iyyah with a meaning befitting Allah while denying physical accompaniment, indwelling, proximity by distance or co-location.
entries.khalafReading: Ma'iyyah is read by context as knowledge, support, aid, protection or witness, never physical presence in a place.

entries.englishMeaning: Those who pledge allegiance to you are in truth pledging allegiance to Allah; Allah's authority is over their pledge. Whoever breaks it only harms himself, while whoever fulfills the covenant he made with Allah will be granted an immense reward.
entries.editorialNote: Yad Allah fawqa aydihim is rendered as divine authority over the covenant, not a bodily hand or spatial position.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the revealed expression with a meaning befitting Allah while denying limbs, hands, parts, bodily form or created instruments.
entries.khalafReading: Yad and related expressions are read contextually as power, authority, generosity, care or disposal according to the verse, not as bodily hands.

entries.englishMeaning: We created the human being and know what his soul whispers to him; Our knowledge of him is nearer than his jugular vein.
entries.editorialNote: The verse begins with divine knowledge, so nearness is rendered as nearness of knowledge rather than spatial distance.
entries.salafReading: Affirm divine nearness with a meaning befitting Allah while denying distance, physical proximity, contact or location.
entries.khalafReading: Nearness is read contextually through knowledge, response, power, care or the nearness of appointed angels, not spatial distance.

entries.englishMeaning: We have built the heaven with might, and We it is Who make the vast extent (thereof).
entries.editorialNote: The wording is reviewed so that yad-related expressions denote power, disposal, care, generosity, support or authority according to context, without attributing limbs or bodily hands to Allah.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the revealed wording according to a meaning befitting Allah while maintaining tanzih: Allah does not resemble creation and is not described by body, limbs, composition, place, direction, movement, change, or a created modality.
entries.khalafReading: Contextual ta’wil assigns a non-bodily meaning appropriate to the verse—such as power, disposal, care, bounty, support or authority—while the Salaf reading maintains tanzih.

entries.englishMeaning: Be patient with your Lord's decree, for you are under Our care; glorify your Lord with praise when you rise.
entries.editorialNote: Bi-a'yunina is rendered as care and protection.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the revealed wording while denying eyes as bodily organs, parts or created instruments.
entries.khalafReading: Ayn and a'yun wording is read contextually as care, protection and oversight, without bodily implication.

entries.englishMeaning: It sailed under Our care, as a reward for the one who had been rejected.
entries.editorialNote: Bi-a'yunina is rendered as care, not physical sight organs.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the revealed wording while denying eyes as bodily organs, parts or created instruments.
entries.khalafReading: Ayn and a'yun wording is read contextually as care, protection and oversight, without bodily implication.

entries.englishMeaning: Only your Lord, Possessor of Majesty and Honour, remains forever.
entries.editorialNote: Wajh rabbika is rendered through Allah Himself, consistent with the guide's allowance of Self as a non-bodily meaning.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the revealed wajh wording with a meaning befitting Allah while denying a bodily face, countenance, direction or created form.
entries.khalafReading: Wajh is read contextually through meanings such as Allah Himself, His acceptance, His Dominion or the qiblah, as the supplied guide and verse context permit.

entries.englishMeaning: Our appointed angels are nearer to the dying person than you are, though you do not see them.
entries.editorialNote: The contextual reading avoids attributing spatial proximity to Allah; this remains explicitly provisional pending qualified scholarly review.
entries.salafReading: Affirm divine nearness with a meaning befitting Allah while denying distance, physical proximity, contact or location.
entries.khalafReading: Nearness is read contextually through knowledge, response, power, care or the nearness of appointed angels, not spatial distance.

entries.englishMeaning: He is the One Who created the heavens and the earth in six days; then He exercises absolute dominion over and subjugates the Throne, without sitting, place, direction, movement, or bodily modality. He knows what enters the earth and what comes out of it, what descends from the heaven and what ascends into it. He knows you wherever you are. Allah sees all that you do.
entries.editorialNote: This is one of the Qur'anic istiwa-over-the-Throne passages. Following the supplied guide's treatment of 20:5, the English uses the contextual ta'wil of absolute dominion/subjugation and explicitly rejects sitting, place, direction, movement and bodily modality.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the revealed istiwa according to a meaning befitting Allah while denying sitting, place, direction, movement, bodily form and every created modality.
entries.khalafReading: Contextual ta'wil: istiwa over the Throne is rendered as Allah's absolute dominion and subjugation, never sitting, spatial establishment or movement. Allah's attribute of subjugation is not temporally originated.
entries.guideSpecificMeaning: Allah knows about you wherever you are.

entries.englishMeaning: So that the People of the Scripture may know that they control nothing of Allah's bounty, and that all bounty is in Allah's disposal to grant to whom He wills. Allah is the Possessor of immense bounty.
entries.editorialNote: Bi-yad Allah is rendered as disposal and granting.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the revealed expression with a meaning befitting Allah while denying limbs, hands, parts, bodily form or created instruments.
entries.khalafReading: Yad and related expressions are read contextually as power, authority, generosity, care or disposal according to the verse, not as bodily hands.

entries.englishMeaning: Do you not see that Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on earth? No three hold secret counsel except that He knows them completely, nor five except that He knows them completely, nor fewer or more, except that He knows them wherever they are. Then on the Day of Resurrection He will inform them of what they did. Surely Allah knows all things.
entries.editorialNote: The verse itself opens and closes with divine knowledge; 'He is with them' is rendered as knowledge, not physical presence.
entries.salafReading: Affirm divine ma'iyyah with a meaning befitting Allah while denying physical accompaniment, indwelling, proximity by distance or co-location.
entries.khalafReading: Ma'iyyah is read by context as knowledge, support, aid, protection or witness, never physical presence in a place.

entries.englishMeaning: Thou wilt not find folk who believe in Allah and the Last Day loving those who oppose Allah and His messenger, even though they be their fathers or their sons or their brethren or their clan. As for such, He hath written faith upon their hearts and hath strengthened them with support granted by Him, and He will bring them into Gardens underneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide. Allah is well pleased with them, and they are well pleased with Him. They are Allah's party. Lo! is it not Allah's party who are the successful?
entries.editorialNote: Possessive/from-Him spirit language is rendered as a created spirit, an attribution of honour, command or divine support; it never means a part, soul or component of Allah.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the revealed wording according to a meaning befitting Allah while maintaining tanzih: Allah does not resemble creation and is not described by body, limbs, composition, place, direction, movement, change, or a created modality.
entries.khalafReading: Contextual ta’wil: the spirit is created and may be attributed to Allah by honour, command, creation or support; Allah is not composed of parts and has no soul.

entries.englishMeaning: He is the One Who expelled from their homes at the first exile those among the People of the Scripture who disbelieved. You did not think they would leave, and they thought their fortresses would protect them from Allah; but Allah's decree reached them from where they did not expect and cast terror into their hearts. They demolished their homes with their own hands and the hands of the believers. So take warning, people of insight.
entries.editorialNote: The baseline 'Allah reached them from a place' is replaced by the reaching of His decree, removing spatial movement.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the revelation while denying movement, transition, arrival from one place to another, place and direction for Allah.
entries.khalafReading: Coming or intervening language is read contextually as the coming of Allah's command, judgment, decree, power or effect, not bodily movement.

entries.englishMeaning: And Mary, daughter of Imran, who guarded her chastity; We caused the honoured created spirit to be blown into her by Our command. She affirmed the words of her Lord and His Books and was among the devout.
entries.editorialNote: The supplied guide rejects any reading in which 'Our spirit' means a part or soul of Allah. It explains the passage through Allah's command to Jibril and a soul honoured by Allah. The SalahOS wording therefore makes createdness and honour explicit.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the revealed wording while categorically denying that Allah has a soul, parts or anything separable from Him.
entries.khalafReading: The guide explains that Allah ordered Jibril to blow the honoured soul by Allah's command; 'Our spirit' is an attribution of honour, not a part of Allah.
entries.guideSpecificMeaning: Allah ordered Jibril to blow the soul which is honorable to Allah.

entries.englishMeaning: Blessed is He Who holds absolute sovereignty over all things, and He is able to do all things.
entries.editorialNote: Bi-yadihi al-mulk is rendered as possession and sovereign control.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the revealed expression with a meaning befitting Allah while denying limbs, hands, parts, bodily form or created instruments.
entries.khalafReading: Yad and related expressions are read contextually as power, authority, generosity, care or disposal according to the verse, not as bodily hands.

entries.englishMeaning: Do you feel secure from the One of supreme status and authority that He will not cause the earth to swallow you as it suddenly convulses?
entries.editorialNote: Man fi al-sama is rendered without making the heaven a place for Allah.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the verse while categorically denying that the heaven contains Allah or is a place for Him.
entries.khalafReading: The expression is read through Allah's supreme status and authority or the heavenly agents under His command, not residence in the sky.

entries.englishMeaning: Or do you feel secure from the One of supreme status and authority that He will not send against you a storm of stones? Then you will know how My warning was.
entries.editorialNote: Man fi al-sama is rendered through supreme status and authority, not residence in the sky.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the verse while categorically denying that the heaven contains Allah or is a place for Him.
entries.khalafReading: The expression is read through Allah's supreme status and authority or the heavenly agents under His command, not residence in the sky.

entries.englishMeaning: On the Day of anguish and hardship, they will be called to prostrate, but they will not be able.
entries.editorialNote: The supplied guide reports the explanation of saq as hardship and the verse as referring to a day of anguish and hardship; it attributes this explanation to Ibn Abbas and other early scholars.
entries.salafReading: The supplied guide records early Salaf authorities explaining the expression without attributing a bodily shin to Allah.
entries.khalafReading: Saq is explained contextually as hardship or severe anguish.
entries.guideSpecificMeaning: A day of anguish and hardship.

entries.englishMeaning: I grant them respite; surely My measured requital is firm.
entries.editorialNote: The divine kayd is rendered as firm measured requital rather than a human-style scheme or deception.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the revealed wording according to a meaning befitting Allah while denying deception, deficiency, injustice or any created moral defect.
entries.khalafReading: Contextual ta'wil: divine kayd is the firm counteraction and measured requital by which wrongdoers are taken to account.

entries.englishMeaning: The angels and the Spirit ascend by His command in a day whose measure is fifty thousand years.
entries.editorialNote: The ascent is rendered as occurring by Allah's command, without implying that Allah occupies a place.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the ascent wording while denying that Allah occupies a destination, place or direction to which created things physically travel.
entries.khalafReading: Ascent is read contextually as being raised by Allah's command, to His acceptance, judgment or an appointed station, without locating Allah.

entries.englishMeaning: So that He knows that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord. His knowledge encompasses all that is with them, and He has counted all things exactly.
entries.editorialNote: The Arabic ahata is rendered through perfect knowledge, not bodily or spatial surrounding. This follows the same tanzih rule the supplied guide applies to encompassing language such as 41:54.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the revealed wording with a meaning befitting Allah while denying physical surrounding, enclosure, spatial extension, containment, or location.
entries.khalafReading: Contextual ta'wil: Allah's encompassing here is His complete knowledge of all that is with the messengers; it is not physical enclosure.

entries.englishMeaning: Beholding their Lord, without direction or modality.
entries.editorialNote: The Ashari-Maturidi project guide specifically requires Qur'an 75:22–23 to affirm the believers' seeing of Allah in the Hereafter while rejecting direction and modality. This wording avoids the directional suggestion that can arise from an unqualified 'looking toward'.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the promised ru'yah as revealed, while denying direction, distance, bodily encounter, containment, and every created modality.
entries.khalafReading: Contextual clarification: the believers will truly see Allah in the Hereafter, but that seeing is not by facing a direction, spatial distance, or a bodily modality.
entries.guideSpecificMeaning: The believers will see Allah in the Hereafter without direction or modality.

entries.englishMeaning: (Saying): We feed you, for the sake of Allah only. We wish for no reward nor thanks from you;
entries.editorialNote: The expression is rendered contextually as Allah’s acceptance, pleasure, Dominion, or Allah Himself as the context requires, without attributing a bodily face or created form.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the revealed wording according to a meaning befitting Allah while maintaining tanzih: Allah does not resemble creation and is not described by body, limbs, composition, place, direction, movement, change, or a created modality.
entries.khalafReading: Contextual ta’wil of wajh is selected verse by verse; it may denote qiblah, Dominion, Allah Himself, or seeking Allah’s acceptance and pleasure, never a bodily face.

entries.englishMeaning: Yet Allah's knowledge and power encompass them completely.
entries.editorialNote: Muhīt is rendered through knowledge and power rather than bodily or spatial surrounding.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the revealed wording according to a meaning befitting Allah while maintaining tanzih: Allah does not resemble creation and is not described by body, limbs, composition, place, direction, movement, change, or any created modality.
entries.khalafReading: Contextual ta'wil: Allah encompasses them in knowledge and power, not by physical enclosure or location.

entries.englishMeaning: And I frustrate their plot by a decisive decree.
entries.editorialNote: The divine response to their plotting is rendered as frustrating it by decree, not human-style deceptive plotting.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the revealed wording according to a meaning befitting Allah while denying deception, deficiency, injustice or any created moral defect.
entries.khalafReading: Contextual ta'wil: Allah counters and frustrates the plotters by His decree and just requital; no created defect is attributed to Him.

entries.englishMeaning: And an indication of your Lord's Power comes, and the angels, rank upon rank.
entries.editorialNote: The supplied guide reports an explanation attributed to Imam Ahmad: the coming here is the coming of an indication of Allah's Power, not movement of Allah from one place to another.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the revealed wording while denying movement, transition, place and direction for Allah.
entries.khalafReading: The guide reports the meaning: an indication of the Power of Allah has come.
entries.guideSpecificMeaning: An indication of the Power of Allah has come.

entries.englishMeaning: Except as seeking (to fulfil) the acceptance and pleasure of his Lord Most High.
entries.editorialNote: The expression is rendered contextually as Allah’s acceptance, pleasure, Dominion, or Allah Himself as the context requires, without attributing a bodily face or created form.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the revealed wording according to a meaning befitting Allah while maintaining tanzih: Allah does not resemble creation and is not described by body, limbs, composition, place, direction, movement, change, or a created modality.
entries.khalafReading: Contextual ta’wil of wajh is selected verse by verse; it may denote qiblah, Dominion, Allah Himself, or seeking Allah’s acceptance and pleasure, never a bodily face.

entries.englishMeaning: And there is absolutely nothing equal or comparable to Him.
entries.editorialNote: A governing muhkam foundation in the supplied guide: nothing is equal to Allah.
entries.guideSpecificMeaning: There is nothing which is equal to Him.
